import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Handle NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' by filling with 'None' for better visualization
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None')

# Set a visually appealing style for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a relational plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration, Quality of Sleep,
# Stress Level, and Physical Activity, faceted by Sleep Disorder.
# This allows us to see how these key metrics interact under different sleep disorder conditions.
g = sns.relplot(
    data=df,
    x="Sleep Duration",
    y="Quality of Sleep",
    hue="Stress Level",
    size="Physical Activity Level", # Map physical activity to marker size
    col="Sleep Disorder", # Create separate plots for each sleep disorder category
    col_wrap=2, # Arrange facets into two columns
    kind="scatter", # Specify scatter plot
    height=4, # Height of each facet
    aspect=1.2, # Aspect ratio of each facet
    sizes=(50, 400), # Range of marker sizes for 'Physical Activity Level'
    alpha=0.7, # Transparency of markers
    palette="viridis", # Color palette for 'Stress Level'
    legend="full", # Show full legend for hue and size
    facet_kws={'sharex': False, 'sharey': False} # Allow each facet to have its own x and y limits
)

# Set custom titles and labels for clarity
g.set_axis_labels("Sleep Duration (hours)", "Quality of Sleep (1-10)")
g.set_titles(col_template="{col_name} Sleep Disorder")
g.fig.suptitle("Sleep Metrics: Duration vs. Quality by Stress, Activity, and Disorder", y=1.02, fontsize=16)

# Adjust the layout to prevent titles and labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.98]) # Adjust rectangle to make space for suptitle

# Save the figure as a high-resolution PNG image
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

    col="Sleep Disorder", # Create separate plots for each sleep disorder category
